title: Provenance & versions
summary: Record what an assertion or analysis was derived from and how it became approved.

sections.label: Useful provenance
items: Exact supporting passage and retained qualifiers.
Extraction/mapping activity and model/tool version where used.
Revisions of the inputs that affect the result, such as code, data, schemas, or ontology and shapes where used.

sections.label: Established vocabulary
sections.text: W3C PROV-O provides entities, activities, agents, derivation, and attribution concepts. Apply the principles to existing mechanisms; an ontology rewrite is not a prerequisite.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: A past answer or finding can be reproduced from its input versions and process evidence.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended workflow use: Requirements and evidence, Tests and review, Observe and improve. Use when recording the evidence behind a requirement, reviewing a result and correcting dependent knowledge after its sources or process change. This is an Atlas recommendation reviewed on 2026-10-15, not a mandatory process or an observed execution result.
Check output to obtain: Produce a result-to-source record with exact input revisions, supporting passages and derivation activity.
Check output to obtain: Reconstruct one past conclusion from the recorded inputs and identify any missing artifact.
Check output to obtain: Distinguish source publication, execution, review and approval timestamps, with the actual responsible owner.

catalog.applicability: Use this when you need to record what an assertion, answer or analysis was derived from, which input versions affected it and who approved it. Apply PROV-O principles to existing mechanisms, since an ontology rewrite is not a prerequisite.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
